technical-data.invention-title: MODULE SCHEDULING WITH A TIME INTERVAL AND ENDING TIME
PROGRAMMATION DE MODULES AVEC INTERVALLE HORAIRE ET HEURE DE FIN

abstract.p: A system and method implemented in an interactive television system for scheduling delivery of modules of interactive television applications from a broadcast station to a receiving station. In one embodiment, the system calculates a start time from a predetermined end time and transmission interval for a module. In other embodiments, a transmission interval may be calculated instead of being predetermined, or all of the scheduling information may be explicitly provided to the broadcast station. The module is packetized and transmission of the packets for the module is begun at the corresponding start time. All of the packets except the last packet are transmitted within the transmission interval (i.e., between the start time and the delivery time.) The greater the transmission interval, the greater the flexibility the broadcast station has to schedule delivery of the packets and modules. The last packet is held until the scheduled delivery time and is then transmitted. Because a module is considered to have been delivered to the receiving station when the last packet is received, the delivery time of the module is controllable to within the limits of the last packet's delivery.

L'invention se rapporte à un système et à un procédé mis en oeuvre dans un système de télévision interactive pour programmer le transfert de modules d'applications de télévision interactive, d'une station de diffusion à une station de réception. Dans une réalisation, le système calcule une heure de début à partir d'une heure de fin préétablie et un intervalle de transmission pour un module. Dans d'autres réalisations, un intervalle de transmission peut être calculé plutôt que préétabli, ou toutes les informations de programmation peuvent être explicitement fournies à la station de diffusion. Le module est divisé en paquets et la transmission des paquets associés au module commence à l'heure de début correspondante. Tous les paquets à l'exception du dernier sont émis pendant l'intervalle de transmission (c'est à dire, entre l'heure de début et l'heure de transfert). Plus l'intervalle de transmission est grand, plus la station de diffusion dispose d'une souplesse importante pour programmer le transfert des paquets et des modules. Le dernier paquet est retenu jusqu'à l'heure de fin programmée puis il est émis. Du fait qu'un module est considéré comme transféré à la station de réception lorsque le dernier paquet a été reçu, l'heure de remise du module peut être ajustée à l'intérieur des limites du transfert du dernier paquet.

description.p: TITLE: MODULE SCHEDULING WITH A TIME INTERVAL AND ENDING TIME
BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
1 Field of the Invention
The invention relates to interactive television systems and more particularly to scheduling the delivery of application modules which are to be transmitted to an interactive television receiver

2. Description of the Related Art Interactive television systems are capable of displaying text and graphic images in addition to typical video program streams and are useful to provide a number of services and interactive applications to viewers. Interactive television systems are also capable of registeπng viewer actions m response to the audio and video information presented by the system. Features of interactive television include a variety of marketing, entertainment and educational capabilities such as allowing a user to interact with televised programs by ordenng advertised products or services, competing against contestants in a game show, or requesting specialized information regarding particular programs

Typically, a broadcast service provider generates an interactive television signal for transmission to a viewer's television. The interactive television signal includes an interactive portion consisting of application code or control information, as well as an audio-video portion consisting of a television program. The broadcast service provider combines the audio-video and interactive portions mto a single signal for transmission to a receiver connected to the user's television The signal is generally compressed prior to transmission and transmitted through typical broadcast channels, such as cable television (CATV) lines or direct satellite transmission systems

The interactive functionality of the television is controlled by a set-top box connected to the television. The set-top box receives the signal transmitted by the broadcast service provider, separates the interactive portion from the audio-video portion and decompresses the respective portions of the signal The set-top box uses the interactive information to, for example, execute an application while the audio- video information is transmitted to the television The set-top box may combine the audio-video mformation with interactive graphics or audio generated by the interactive application prior to transmitting the mformation to the television. The interactive graphics and audio may present additional information to the viewer or may prompt the viewer for input. The set-top box may provide viewer input or other mformation to the broadcast service provider via a modem connection.

Interactive television applications may consist of a set of program modules. The entire set of modules is transmitted via the broadcast channel to the set-top box and the application is executed. The modules are packetized before they are transmitted to the receiving station. That is, the modules are broken down into smaller pieces of mformation which are then formatted for transmission over the broadcast channel or other transmission medium. The packets containing the pieces of a particular module may be transmitted consecutively, or they may be interspersed with packets containing portions of other modules. The packets arrive at a receiving station, where they are accumulated When the last packet containing part of a particular module is received, that module is considered to have been received. Consequently, if it is necessary to deliver
a module to a receiving station at a particular time, transmission of the module must begm at a time which is sufficiently early to allow transmission of all the packets contammg portions of the module before the required delivery time

The simple way of schedulmg transmission of a module is to calculate (approximately) the time required to deliver the entire module and subtractmg this from the scheduled delivery time The duration of the transmission can be determined by dividing the size of the module by the bit rate at which its packets will be transmitted This method schedulmg the modules requires that the broadcast channel be reserved for this particular module and that all of the module's packets be transmitted consecutively This constraint considerably mcreases the difficulty of schedulmg the potentially large number of modules which may be required for an application If packets of more than one module must be sent at the same time, the method fails It may also be difficult, or even impossible, to schedule modules for delivery at or near the same time Further, the accuracy with which the delivery tune of a single module can be scheduled using this method is limited because, although the start time of the transmission is known, the actual duration of the transmission can only be estimated An improved mechanism for schedulmg delivery of the modules would therefore be desirable
SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

The invention comprises a system and method for schedulmg the delivery of packetized modules from a transmitting station to a receiving station The mvention provides a mechanism which allows flexibility m schedulmg delivery of modules while maintaining accurate determination of delivery times The transmitt g station begins transmission of a given module's packets at a time which is sufficiently early that all of the packets can be delivered before the module's scheduled delivery time Transmission of the last packet is held until the scheduled delivery time and then transmitted Because the module is considered to have been received at the receiving station when the last packet is received, the module's actual delivery time can be scheduled with the accuracy achievable with a smgle packet mstead of the accuracy achievable when transmittmg an entire module

One embodiment of the mvention compπses an interactive television system havmg a transmitting station (referred to herein as a broadcast station) which is coupled to one or more receiving stations by a broadcast channel The broadcast station and receiving stations may also be coupled by point-to-point channels The broadcast station is configured to format application modules or other data mto packets (I e , "packetize" them) and transmit the packets to the receivmg station via the broadcast or point-to-point channels The receiving station mcludes a set-top box configured to receive and store the packets until the entire module has been received

The broadcast station contains a scheduler The scheduler is provided with predetermined tunes at which modules should be delivered from the broadcast station to the receivmg station In one embodiment, a transmission interval is also provided to the scheduler The mterval is at least as long and preferably greater than the time which would be required to transmit the module's packets consecutively The greater the transmission interval, the more flexibility the scheduler has to deliver the module's packets An additional amount of flexibility m schedulmg can be achieved by allowing the delivery of the module to fall within a range around the delivery time (This flexibility is particularly helpful in instances m which transmission of two or
more modules is overlapped ) The scheduler calculates a transmission start time based on the scheduled delivery time and the transmission mterval The scheduler begms transmission of the module at the calculated start time and completes transmission of all but the last packet before the scheduled delivery time At the scheduled delivery time, the last packet is transmitted When this packet is received by the receiving station, the complete module has been received and the actual delivery tune is established

In an alternate embodiment, the transmission mterval may also be calculated If only a smgle module is to be transmitted, the transmission mterval may be calculated by dividing the size of the module by the transmission bit rate If there are several modules to be transmitted simultaneously, the transmission mterval may be calculated by dividing the aggregate size of the modules by the transmission bit rate If the transmission of several modules is to be overlapped, the transmission mtervals requued to deliver the modules mdividually may be mcreased by a multiplier to account for the sharing of the delivery channel by the modules Any other suitable method may also be used to calculate the transmission mterval In any case, all of the packets, except the last packet, of each scheduled module are transmitted beginning at the respectively calculated start tunes Smce the delivery tune of a module is the delivery tune of the corresponding last packet, the delivery times of the modules can be scheduled with a much greater accuracy than m the pπor art The modules may also be transmitted so that their delivery times are nearly the same, even when the modules are very large

In another embodiment, the schedulmg and even the packetization of the modules may be done in advance The producer of a module may deliver a pre-scheduled and pre-packetized version of the module to the broadcast station, which would then multiplex the module's packets with other packets and transmit them accordmg to the predetermmed schedule The other packets could contam audio, video, applications, or other types of mformation The pre-scheduled, pre-packetized version of the module may itself mclude packets of audio, video, applications or other mformation That is, these other packets may be included in the pre- scheduled, pre-packetized version of the module pπor to delivery to the broadcast station

DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE PREFERRED EMBODIMENT

One embodiment of the invention is descnbed below In this embodiment, an interactive television receiving station accepts an audio-video-interactive signal via a broadcast channel such as duect satellite transmission. ("Duect" satellite transmission as used herem contemplates transmissions received by the mteractive television receiver, more particularly by its antenna, duectly from the satellite.) The audio-video- mteractive signal contams television programs or similar audio- video content, as well as mteractive content such as control signals or mteractive applications. ("Broadcast" is used herem to refer to transmission of a smgle signal to all subscπbmg receivers.) The receivmg station may also be configured to receive signals via a modem channel The signals transmitted via the broadcast and modem channels may embody various modules which compnse components of an mteractive application. The modules can contam any type of data, such as application code, raw data or graphical mformation.

The broadcast station mcludes a scheduler which controls the transmission of the modules to the receivmg station. For each scheduled module, the scheduler is provided with a delivery tune and sufficient mformation to calculate a transmission start time In most cases, the scheduler is provided with a predetermmed transmission mterval for each module, so that determination of a start tune is simply a matter of subtractmg the mterval from the delivery tune. In other cases, the scheduler must calculate the transmission mterval from other mformation, such as the demand for bandwidth on the transmission channels. This mformation may mclude module size, transmission bit rate, and number of modules which are to be transmitted at the same time. In still other cases, the start time, transmission mterval and delivery tune may all be predetermmed and provided to the broadcast station. The scheduler causes all of the packets of a module, except the last packet, to be transmitted between the start tune and the delivery time. The last packet is held until the delivery tune and is then transmitted. The receivmg station may mclude a module manager which tracks the incoming packets and determmes when the last packet is received. When the last packet is received (i.e., at the scheduled delivery tune,) the module is assigned a delivery time and is processed by the receivmg station.

The audio-video-interactive transmission from the broadcast station to the mteractive television receiver compnses a senes of packets As descnbed above, the packets which form a given module are typically tune multiplexed with other mformation. That is, they are mterspersed or mterleaved with other packets The packets of the respective modules need not be multiplexed m any particular ratio (e.g , 1:1.) Referring to Fig. 5, each module 51 has a data segment 52 and a CRC segment 53 The data segment 52 of the module can contam any type of data, such as application code, module duectory mformation or raw data. The CRC segment 53 of each of the module is used for error control and is computed for the entire module 51. Each module 51 normally has a unique identifier. Module 51 is normally broken down mto smaller pieces to facilitate transmission of the module In one embodiment, module 51 is broken down mto transmission units and then packetized (formatted mto packets) for transmission on the broadcast channel. The descnption below is directed to one embodiment of this mechanism which is mtended to be illustrative rather than limiting

Before a module 51 is transmitted, it is formatted mto transmission units 54 Each of the transmission units 54 contains header mformation 55, which uniquely identifies that transmission unit 54 within the stream of transmission units, and data 56 which compnses a portion of the module bemg transmitted. The header 55 contains mformation such as the module ID, module offset and size, which allow the transmission units 54 to be reconstructed mto a complete module. The transmission units 54 compnsmg a particular module 51 may be mterleaved with other transmission units 54 m the transmission stream. The format of the transmission units 54 is dependent upon the transmission medium, but typically employs a senes of packets of fixed length (the last packet may be padded to obtam the proper length.) In one embodiment, the first packet 58 m the series cames the header mformation as well as data for the transmission unit 54 Similar packets carry the remamder of the transmission umt data. In an alternate embodiment, the header packet 58 may be an auxiliary packet which can generate an interrupt m the CPU The auxiliary packet contams mformation to enable the CPU to determine whether the module 51 should be decoded and where it should be loaded mto memory.

It should be noted that, while the foregomg descnption uses the term "packet" m a conventional sense, it is contemplated that the mvention is equally applicable m the transmission of other module segments. The use of this term is therefore mtended to refer to all such subdivisions of the modules.

As descnbed above, the broadcast signal is collected by receivmg station antenna 17 and fed to set-top box 18 Set-top box 18 processes the packetized signal to reconstruct the television programs and mteractive applications embodied m the signal The reconstructed applications are executed m the set-top box, while the reconstructed television programs are passed to the television, where they are displayed. Control system 65 may mclude a microprocessor, micro-controller, digital signal processor (DSP), or some other type of software instruction processmg device. RAM 67 may mclude memory units which are static (e.g., SRAM), dynamic (e.g., DRAM), volatile or non-volatile (e.g., FLASH), as requued to support the functions of the set-top box. When power is applied to the set-top box, control system 65 executes operating system code which is stored m ROM 66. The operating system code executes continuously while the set-top box is powered m the same manner the operating system code of a typical personal computer (PC) and enables the set-top box to act on control mformation and execute mteractive and other applications. The set-top box may also mclude modem 68. Modem 68 provides both a return path by which viewer data can be transmitted to the broadcast station and an alternate path by which the broadcast station can transmit data to the set-top box.

Although the term "set-top box" is used herem, it is understood that this term refers to any receiver or processmg unit for receiving and processmg a transmitted signal and conveymg the processed signal to a television or other monitor. The set-top box may be m a housmg which physically sits on top of a television, it may be m some other location external to the television (e.g., on the side or back of the television or remotely located from the television), or it may be incorporated mto the television itself. Set-top box 18 serves to demodulate the signal received from broadcast station 10 and to separate the components of the signal, such as different television programs and mteractive applications. Similarly, television 19 may be a television or a video monitor employmg any suitable television format (e.g., NTSC or HDTV), or it may be replaced by other devices, such as a video recorder.

The receivmg station is operatively connected to the broadcast station by a broadcast channel. This broadcast channel could utilize vanous transmission media and is contemplated to mclude media such as coaxial cable and free space (e.g., as used for duect satellite transmissions.) The broadcast channel forms a transmission path between the broadcast station and the receivmg station. The broadcast station and receivmg station are also connected by a return path. The return path typically consists of a pau of modems, one m the receivmg station and one m the broadcast station, each connected to a standard telephone lme Other means for establishing a return path, e g., usmg a portion of the bandwidth of the transmission path, are also contemplated
Referring to Figs. 7a and 7b, a diagrammatic representation of the signal transmitted from broadcast station 10 to receivmg station 20 is shown. The figures depict the packets of two modules transmitted m a consecutive mode of operation (Fig. 7a) and a simultaneous mode of operation (Fig. 7b). In Fig. 7a, all of the packets of a smgle module (Mod. 1) are to transmitted consecutively The scheduler can schedule transmission of the packets by determining the transmission mterval (I,) and subtractmg this mterval from the scheduled delivery tune (D,) to get start tune (S,). I, can be explicitly provided to the scheduler, or it can be calculated, for example, by dividing the module size by the transmission bit rate as explamed above. Transmission of the packets can therefore begm at S, and should be complete m time to deliver the last packet at Dl. This assumes that no errors occur and no retransmissions are requued. I, can alternatively be calculated to mclude sufficient tune to allow for errors and retransmissions. A second module (Mod. 2) can be scheduled m the same manner for transmission after the first module. While this mode of operation may appear to be similar to schedulmg m the pπor art, it is distinct because the last packet of each module is held until the delivery time. Thus, if the transmission mterval is greater than the minimum tune required to transmit all of the packets, the same delivery tune (Dl, D2) is maintained, while m pπor art systems the delivery tune would vary with the unused tune m the mterval

In another mode of operation, illustrated m Fig 7b, two modules can be transmitted simultaneously ("Simultaneously," as used here, refers to the overlappmg of at least a portion of the modules and does not require that the transmission of the respective modules' packets begm and end at the same tune.) In this figure, both modules are scheduled for delivery at approximately the same time (D„ D2). For each module, a transmission mterval is determmed. Agam, the mterval can be explicitly provided, or it can be calculated by the scheduler based on bandwidth demand. In this mstance, each module has an equal mterval, resulting m start tunes (S,, S2) which are approximately the same. As noted above, m vanous embodiments, any or all of the schedulmg mformation may be explicitly provided to the broadcast station. Further, the packets depicted as a smgle module m Figs. 7a and 7b may alternately consist of pre-multrplexed packets containing modules, audio, video or other mformation. The pre-multrplexed packets may then be re-multiplexed by the broadcast station or simply transmitted consecutively

The signal which embodies the packets is received by set- top box 18. Set- top box 18 demultiplexes the packets and reconstructs the respective television programs and modules. As noted above, the modules are stored m RAM 67, where they are available for use by applications executmg m the control system 65. The set- top box may employ a secunty mechanism to ensure that the carousels and/or particular modules which are bemg downloaded are authentic. A certificate system may be used to ensure that the modules are produced by authorized producers and that the modules have not been altered before bemg received by the set-top box.

In one embodiment, the module manager unit controls delivery, access and other functions of the set- top box which relate to the modules. The module manager unit may be implemented m software, hardware or a combmation of both as a matter of design choice The module manager unit monitors the channels through which it is coupled to the broadcast station. In one embodiment, all the packets of a particular module must be transmitted over the same channel. In other embodiments, the module manager unit
may be configured to accept packets of a particular module from multiple channels (e.g., both a broadcast channel and a pomt-to-pomt channel.)

As the packets of one or more modules are transmitted to the set-top box, the module manager unit stores the packets so they can be reconstructed mto the respective modules. The module manager unit also momtors the packets to determine whether the last packet of a module has been received. When the last packet of a module is received, the delivery tune of the module is recorded. The module can then be reconstructed from its packets and processed by the set-top box. If the module is part of an application, it may be loaded mto memory for execution. If the module consists of graphical rnformanon, it may simply be displayed on the television coupled to the set-top box.
